text: A tumbling window trigger fires at a periodic interval from a specified start time, while genuinely retaining state — the windows are fixed-size, non-overlapping, and contiguous, covering time continuously with no gaps and no overlap at all. Where a Schedule trigger has a many-to-many relationship with pipelines, this one has a strict one-to-one relationship — it can only ever reference a single pipeline.

Three real properties make it genuinely heavier, and genuinely more reliable. Delay controls how long the trigger waits past a window's due time before actually firing, without shifting the window itself. Max concurrency caps how many windows can run simultaneously, anywhere from one to fifty. And retry policy automatically retries a failed pipeline run using the exact same input parameters, with no manual intervention required at all.

Set a start time in the past, and a tumbling window trigger automatically generates every missed window between then and now, in order, from oldest to newest, honoring max concurrency the entire way. Genuinely useful for a brand-new pipeline that needs to process months of historical data on its very first real run.

Compared to a Schedule trigger, this one supports genuine backfill, guarantees no gaps at all, includes a built-in retry policy, and its own run state actually reflects whether the underlying pipeline genuinely succeeded or failed — not just whether it started. Reach for this specifically when you need reliable, gap-free, retryable time-series processing, not just run this sometime around nine AM.
